name: Felix (procurator)
title: The Roman procurator who postponed justice
summary: Marcus Antonius Felix was a Roman procurator over Judea who held the apostle Paul imprisoned for two years. He was known for his brutal rule and his fear of the gospel's message about righteousness and the coming judgment, yet he kept Paul in prison to please the Jews and in hope of receiving a bribe.

keyEvents.title: Paul brought before Felix
keyEvents.description: The apostle Paul was taken from Jerusalem to Caesarea and brought before procurator Felix after the Romans rescued him from a Jewish conspiracy.

keyEvents.title: The trial of Paul
keyEvents.description: The high priest Ananias and the orator Tertullus accused Paul before Felix, but Paul defended himself by explaining that he worshiped God and believed in the Scriptures.

keyEvents.title: Felix and Drusilla hear Paul
keyEvents.description: Felix and his Jewish wife Drusilla sent for Paul to hear him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.

keyEvents.title: Felix is frightened by the message
keyEvents.description: When Paulus spoke about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix was seized with fear and sent Paulus away, while at the same time hoping for a bribe.

keyEvents.title: Paulus is held captive for two years
keyEvents.description: Felix kept Paulus in prison for two years without a verdict, to win favor with the Jews. When he was succeeded by Porcius Festus, he left Paulus in prison.
